R7BE-moose-backcountry-0003.name: 180 m SW of Akie River
R7BE-moose-backcountry-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R7BE-moose-backcountry-0003.parkWhat: pull off on Akie M/L (gravel road)

evidence.t: 3 wetlands within 2 km; nearest 1.2 ha, right here.
Burn from 2023 (fire G60325), right here: browse.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, about 272 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 57.33157, -124.94817, pull off on Akie M/L (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 30 km E, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 2,166 m, about 807 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m N of the spot at 977 m (57.32374, -124.45811). Water: Akie River 110 m NE (estimate).
Hunt: moose, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass the wetland and cutblock edges at dawn and dusk. Move slowly, stop often (Tip).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-41, Region 7A. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2023-09-20, closures 2026-10-16.
R7BE-moose-backcountry-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 7-41: about 170 hunter days a year for moose (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.02 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
